You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Do you mean battles filtered by (a) number of ships lost, (b) number of casualties (killed/injured), or (c) loss of a specific ship/name/type? Tell me which and the numeric threshold or ship name/type and I will return the exact query. Meanwhile, here are example queries for the common interpretations — replace the numbers/names as needed.

```sql
-- 1) Battles with exactly N ships lost (replace 3 with the desired number)
SELECT b.id, b.name, b.date, COUNT(s.id) AS ships_lost
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING COUNT(s.id) = 3;

-- 2) Battles with at least N total casualties (killed + injured) caused by ships lost in that battle
-- (replace 10 with desired threshold)
SELECT b.id, b.name, b.date,
       COALESCE(SUM(d.killed),0) AS total_killed,
       COALESCE(SUM(d.injured),0) AS total_injured,
       COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(d.killed,0) + COALESCE(d.injured,0)),0) AS total_casualties
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(d.killed,0) + COALESCE(d.injured,0)),0) >= 10;

-- 3) Battles where a specific ship (by name) was lost (replace 'USS Example' with ship name)
SELECT DISTINCT b.id, b.name, b.date
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
WHERE s.name = 'USS Example';
```

Which of these (or a different definition) do you want? Specify the number or ship/name/type and I'll adapt.
the losses should specifically include 'Brig' type ships

Do you mean battles where at least one lost ship is a Brig, or battles where all lost ships are Brigs (or something else, e.g., at least N Brigs lost)? Below I assume "include" = at least one Brig lost and return battles with counts (total ships lost and number of Brigs lost). If you want a different variant, tell me which.

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  COUNT(s.id) AS total_ships_lost,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.ship_type = 'Brig' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS brig_ships_lost
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.ship_type = 'Brig' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 1;
```
also need the unique identifiers for these battles

Here's the query including the battle unique identifier (battle_id):

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  COUNT(s.id) AS total_ships_lost,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.ship_type = 'Brig' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS brig_ships_lost
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.ship_type = 'Brig' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 1;
```
also need the names of the battles in the results

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date,
  COUNT(s.id) AS total_ships_lost,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.ship_type = 'Brig' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS brig_ships_lost
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.ship_type = 'Brig' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 1;
```
